extracted.intended_audience: applicants submitting NIH grant applications (researchers seeking CSR review)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applicants on completing the CSR Assignment Request Form to suggest scientific review groups (study sections), awarding components, conflicts of interest, and reviewer expertise for NIH grant applications. Explains how CSR uses that information and how to identify appropriate study sections and awarding components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of the Assignment Request Form
rubrics_metrics.description: The form allows you to: Express a preference for a particular scientific review group (or “study section”); Express a preference for a specific awarding component (an NIH Institute or Center); Let us know of potential reviewers who you feel might have a conflict of interest with your application; Describe the expertise needed to review your application; do not provide names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the form to communicate preferences for study section and awarding component, to flag potential conflicts of interest, and to describe needed reviewer expertise. Explicit instruction: do not provide names of potential reviewers when describing expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form optionality and cover letter rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the form required? No, but assignment suggestions made through the cover letter will not be considered. There is also no requirement that you complete all fields in the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completing the Assignment Request Form is optional; do not rely on cover letter assignment suggestions because CSR will not consider them. Fields on the form may be left blank if not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR use of applicant-provided assignment information
rubrics_metrics.description: We carefully consider all information you provide in making assignments to scientific review groups (study sections) and awarding components, in recruiting appropriate reviewers, and in managing conflicts of interest. We will try to accommodate your suggestions if they are appropriate and possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on the form informs multiple processes (assignment, reviewer recruitment, COI management). CSR staff weigh applicant suggestions against policies and practical constraints and will attempt accommodation when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary criteria for assigning applications to scientific review groups
rubrics_metrics.description: We assign applications to scientific review groups based on the fit between published guidelines for review groups and your application. In assessing fit, we typically consider the abstract, specific aims, broader goals, and methods used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When suggesting a study section, ensure the abstract, specific aims, goals, and methods align with that study section's published guidelines; CSR uses those application elements to assess fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest considered in assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment to a review group also takes into consideration conflicts of interest between key personnel on an application and members of a review group. Your suggestions made via the Assignment Request Form help us to consider the full range of factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSR will factor known or potential conflicts between key personnel and study section members into assignment decisions. Use the form to report possible conflicts to help CSR assess assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section overlap and staff final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Our review groups have some overlap, so more than one might have the expertise to review your application. Our scientific staff make the final assignment after they carefully consider your suggestions in light of NIH policies. The review location for some applications is predetermined, such as those submitted under a request for applications (RFA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware multiple study sections may be appropriate; CSR staff will choose the best fit consistent with NIH policies. Some mechanisms (e.g., RFAs) require predetermined review locations and cannot be changed by applicant preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to identify a potential scientific review group (study section)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can search for a CSR review group by searching for topics or using the CSR Assisted Referral Tool. Examine recent study section rosters to gauge the scope of the group. Note that rosters change over time as we recruit reviewers based on the scientific content of the applications. Consider seeking guidance from an NIH Institute or Center program officer (PO). Use the NIH RePORTER database to identify the study sections that reviewed successful applications in your field. Please pay attention to recent applications and be aware that our study section guidelines are regularly updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical methods: topic search, CSR Assisted Referral Tool, review recent rosters, consult program officers, and use NIH RePORTER to see which study sections handled similar successful applications. Check for recent updates to rosters and guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to identify a potential awarding component
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also request that your application be assigned to an awarding component you think would have the most interest in your research. It's a good idea to contact one or more program officers for guidance before you submit. You can identify NIH program officers via staff listings on NIH Institute and Center web sites. You should also look at the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) you will use to submit your application. Applications cannot be assigned to an institute or center that does not participate in the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before requesting an awarding component, contact program officers for advice, verify participation via IC staff listings and the NOFO, and ensure the chosen institute actually participates in the funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting potential reviewer bias or conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Assignment Request Form to tell us if you know of a potential reviewer who you believe could not provide an impartial review. Rosters are typically posted online 30 days before the review meeting. If you see a reviewer on it who might have a conflict of interest with your application, contact your scientific review officer (SRO) as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected conflicts both on the form and by contacting the SRO promptly if you notice potential conflicts on posted rosters. Timing matters: rosters are posted ~30 days before meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as bias and SRO handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A researcher in your own field who holds a different scientific opinion is not automatically considered biased. These individuals usually provide excellent reviews because they understand the scientific issues. Your SRO will consider the situation and make the final decision. If he/she agrees that there is a conflict, the reviewer will not be assigned to your application and will not be in the room when it's discussed. (SROs will only be able to confirm that NIH policy was followed and will not be able to tell you if specific people were placed in conflict.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume disagreement equals bias; the SRO evaluates alleged bias and enforces COI policy. If a COI is confirmed, the reviewer is excluded from assignment and discussion; SROs cannot disclose specifics beyond policy adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction: Describe expertise needed — do not name reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Assignment Request Form to tell us about specific expertise needed to review your application. Do not provide names of potential reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When indicating desired expertise, focus on topical or methodological expertise rather than listing individuals. Naming potential reviewers is explicitly prohibited in this section.
